https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/ukraine-w.text: Warren Murray with Guardian writers and agencies Updated Mon, 27 July 2026 at 12:54 am UTC 0 Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Donald Trump are due to meet in Washington on Tuesday. Ukrainian and US teams have reportedly discussed offering Vladimir Putin a ceasefire in their air war.Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP Ukrainian and US officials have discussed a proposal to offer Russia an air ceasefire , the Reuters news agency has reported, citing a Ukrainian source. Volodymyr Zelenskyy is due to meet Donald Trump , the US president, in Washington on Tuesday. The Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said on ⁠Sunday that Russia considered it premature to comment on any such ceasefire proposal. “We do not know how credible these reports are or where they come from. These are newspaper reports and nothing more. Therefore, it is premature to comment on them at this stage,” the Interfax news agency quoted Peskov as saying. “We have heard statements that some new formulas may be possible. We still need to learn ​more about them … What happens next will depend on how closely they correspond to our interests.” Romania said it was summoning Russia’s ambassador after the Nato member’s military shot down a third drone in as many days . A Romanian F-16 fighter jet shot down the drone over the Black Sea, five minutes after it entered the country’s airspace, said Romania’s defence minister, Radu Miruță. The foreign minister, Oana Țoiu, condemned “repeated violations”. The Romanian president, Nicușor Dan, said that according to an investigation, a drone shot down on Friday was a “ Shahed model used by the Russian Federation in its war of aggression against Ukraine”. Investigations into drones shot down on Saturday and Sunday continued, he said. The Golden Leo, an international cargo vessel, sank off the coast of ⁠Ukraine’s Black Sea port of Odesa on Sunday , a week after Ukrainian ⁠officials said ⁠it ​had been struck by Russian forces. Nine ⁠crew members were killed in the ​attack while eight ‌were evacuated to safety. The ‌ship had left the ‌port of Chornomorsk with a cargo of corn when it was shelled by Russian forces on 19 July. Russia’s defence ministry ⁠said on Sunday that its forces had ⁠struck Ukrainian ⁠ports ​and shipping. Russia claimed the container terminal ‌at Chornomorsk, near ‌Odesa, handled “military cargoes”. Russia launched seven ballistic missiles and 136 drones at Ukraine overnight into Sunday, the Ukrainian air force said. In the northern Ukrainian city of Chernihiv, a Russian drone hit ⁠a supermarket, killing two people – including a nine-year-old child – and wounding 25, emergency services said. In the eastern city of Kharkiv, one person was killed and 16 others required medical attention ‌after a daytime drone attack, said the mayor, Ihor Terekhov. A glide bomb attack killed one person and wounded six in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia, said the regional governor, Ivan Fedorov. In Kyiv , a fire broke out on the seventh and eighth floors of a multi-storey apartment block in a central district after ‌a missile attack, said the mayor, Vitali Klitschko. Three people were wounded. In Sloviansk, Donetsk region, the national oil and gas company Naftogaz said two of its employees died in a Russian attack while trying to help residents affected by an earlier strike. Russia said ⁠ areas of Ukraine ​under Moscow’s control had also come under attack, with four people killed in a Ukrainian drone strike in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Horlivka. Twelve ⁠people, including two children, were ⁠injured ⁠in drone ​attack on ⁠the Russian city of Belgorod, close ⁠to ​Ukraine’s ‌border, regional authorities ‌said early on Monday. Ukraine denies targeting civilians. Related: Burnham to meet Zelenskyy at UK naval base in show of ‘unwavering’ support Volodymyr Zelenskyy will become Andy Burnham’s first overseas visitor as prime minister , in a visit that Burnham said underlined Britain’s “unwavering” backing for Ukraine, Peter Walker writes . Less than two weeks after Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv for the final foreign visit of his prime ministership, Zelenskyy will on Monday join Burnham at a naval base where Ukrainian forces have been receiving training . According to statistics released by No 10, since Russia’s full invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, total UK support for the country has totalled £25bn, including £16bn in military assistance. Burnham and Zelenskyy are due to discuss joint projects including Stone Cloak, an electronic jammer for which the UK has shared the intellectual property, allowing Ukraine to use the system immediately to prevent Russia shooting down Ukrainian drones. Since being proven on the Ukrainian frontline, the jammers are due to be fitted to new UK weaponry, including cruise missiles. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/10/brit.text: Turkish police arrested a British tourist in the southern resort of Alanya for allegedly spitting on the Turkish flag, media reports said Wednesday.The 58-year-old tourist argued with staff in a hotel then allegedly turned and spat on a flag hanging in the lobby, DHA and IHA news agencies reported, without specifying when it happened.Staff reported the man to police, who detained him and took him to the Alanya courthouse where he was formally arrested on charges of insulting or degrading a symbol of the Turkish state.He was remanded in custody and taken to a local prison just outside the city.There was no immediate response from the British embassy.Under Article 300 of the Turkish penal code, it is illegal to publicly disrespect the Turkish flag -- an offence that can carry a jail term of up to three years.In August 2025, prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into a tourist from Bosnia and Herzegovina for performing a pole dance on a Turkish flagpole in Cappadocia which she posted on social media.The outcome of the case was not clear.

https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/scott.text: A Polish company building seven Scottish ferries announced a major eastern European jobs boost for the project – in the same week that Ferguson Marine cut 70 workers. Ferguson missed out on the £175million taxpayer funded order for seven CalMac electric vessels in 2025 despite “aggressively bidding” for the work. The deal went to Gdansk-based Remontowa, where we learned hundreds of jobs were secured on August 13 via a subcontract to fit out the ships. Five days later Ferguson , in Port Glasgow, axed a quarter of its workforce as a result of a lack of new orders. GMB union convener Alex Logan, who represents hundreds of shipbuilders on the Clyde, said: “We have a worldwide reputation for building small vessels and sending this work overseas makes no sense for the workers, for islanders or for the people of Scotland. They deserve better and this contract should have allowed the yard to seize back a ­reputation for excellence unfairly torn away.” Winning the seven ferry contract had been a key part of nationalised Ferguson’s five-year business plan following delays and cost overruns in the construction of two much larger ferries for CalMac. The 164ft ships are similar to ones delivered in the past by the Scots yard, and could have given it a pipeline of repeatable work lasting several years. But the work went to ­Remontowa, which has now awarded fellow Polish firm Maritime Montering a deal to make interior accommodation for the seven “loch class” ferries. The contract will support hundreds of skilled jobs on top of hundreds more working on the main hulls and ­superstructures being ­assembled in Gdansk. Remontowa has said the contract was awarded following a “competitive international tender process” involving 10 ship interior companies from different countries. Pawel Walczak, head of commercials at Maritime Montering, said it was a “great honour” to win the contract, adding: “Our bid received the highest score following a ­thorough evaluation.” Each ferry will carry up to 150 passengers, five crew and 24 cars, providing essential connections between ­Scotland’s islands, including routes in the Hebrides. With fully ­electric propulsion they will bring increased ­transport capacity while supporting cleaner and more ­sustainable travel for island and rural communities. Delivery of all seven vessels is planned between next year and 2028. Maritime Montering operates from seven countries and employs at least 700 people while Remontowa is one of Europe’s leading shipyards. Remontowa built the CalMac ferries MV Argyle, MV Bute and MV Finlaggan, and was runner-up to Ferguson’s in 2015 when the contracts for Glen Sannox and Glen Rosa were awarded. Price competition from the Gdansk-based firm was blamed for the decline of Ferguson in the early 2000s, and in 2005 SNP politicians joined yard management in lodging a complaint with the European ­Commission about unfair subsidies, which Remontowa and Poland’s government denied. https://www.delfi.lt/en/business/vilnius.text: Delfi EN Delfi Business 2026.09.09 17:47 Vilnius mayor would support bus service ban to Russia and Belarus Translated by Karolis Broga Source: Elta EN Vilnius mayor would support bus service ban to Russia and Belarus PHOTO: Josvydas Elinskas | Elta Follow Delfi on Google As Latvia plans to ban bus services to Russia and Belarus starting next year, Vilnius Mayor Valdas Benkunskas says Lithuania should also approve the move. He says Vilnius municipality has long questioned passenger transport between Russia and Belarus. "I would very much agree with this opinion, because migration or matters related to our border – who we allow in, how we allow in and how we control it – fall within the remit of the national government," Benkunskas told reporters on Wednesday. According to the mayor, some issues, such as how movement across the Belarusian border takes place, certainly raise questions and it should be reviewed how the border operates and who Lithuania allows in. Based on the data from the Lithuanian Transport Safety Administration (LTSA), 29 permits for regular passenger transport between Lithuania and Russia or Belarus, or for transit through Lithuania, are currently in force. These include routes to Minsk, Grodno, Gomel, Lida and Ashmyany. Meanwhile, Latvia plans to ban regular and chartered international bus services to Russia and Belarus, as well as transit through Latvia to those countries. This has been foreseen in legal amendments submitted by the Latvian Transport Ministry to the Government. Currently, one regular bus route runs between Latvia and Russia, the permit for which is valid until 9 January 2027, and there are no plans to extend it. The Latvian Transport Ministry however admits that restriction of regular bus routes from Latvia is not entirely effective as passengers may choose routes with transfers in Estonia and Lithuania, as well as minibus services that are not subject to relevant passenger bus transport regulations. Therefore, Latvia may strive for a joint solution at the level of the Baltic States and the EU.
